clue.text: Cheers one who'd expect to be paid to be an MP?

parts.words: one who'd expect to be paid
parts.note: a pro, a professional, works for pay rather than as an amateur
an MP sits in Parliament, so to sit is to be a member

explanation.surface: A cynical toast to the idea of being paid to serve as a Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a professional sitting in Parliament. Prosit is a German drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a toast said when raising glasses, like the English word for a drinking salute.

clue.text: Fancy knocking off leader for paper?

indicators.note: knocking off the leader means removing the word's first letter

parts.note: a dream is a fancy, an imagined notion

explanation.surface: A pretentious beheading of the head of a paper, perhaps a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking off leader' removes D from DREAM (a fancy). 'Fancy' looks like an adjective; it is the noun meaning a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, conventionally 500 sheets.

clue.text: Mark's house settlement's not finished

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour

indicators.note: not finished means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a colony is a settlement

explanation.surface: A man called Mark has a house in a settlement that is still being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, a punctuation mark. 'Not finished' drops the Y of COLONY. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation symbol, a dot over a comma, separates clauses more strongly than a comma.

clue.text: Lulu's half escaping depression in the old city

indicators.note: escaping means getting out, so those letters leave the phrase

parts.note: the blues is a state of depression or low spirits
half of the name Lulu is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Lulu, the Scottish pop singer, half-escaping her low mood in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escaping' takes LU (half of Lulu) out of THE BLUES (depression). Lulu is a Scottish pop singer, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Light material suffering more snags if not new

indicators.note: suffering means being damaged, so the letters are knocked out of their order
if not means without, so a letter is left out of the pool

explanation.surface: A fine fabric that gets snagged more and more unless it is new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If not' leaves N (new) out of MORE SNAGS, and 'suffering' rearranges the letters MORESAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a very thin, delicate fabric, like the filmy threads of a spider's web.

clue.text: Cynically proposing futile measures — a 'two-fingered salute' way of governing?

parts.note: the two-fingered salute is a rude British hand gesture, the V-sign with the palm inward
politics is the activity of governing

explanation.surface: A jibe at governments that make empty gestures, equated with a rude hand signal.
explanation.walkthrough: A two-fingered salute is a British insulting hand gesture, so it is a gesture; the question mark marks the pun on governing by gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase describes politicians announcing showy measures that will achieve nothing, merely to be seen to act.

clue.text: Lyricist dancing — time for one very popular show

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters step into a new order
for means in place of, so one letter stands where another was

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A lyricist dancing on a hugely popular television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' puts T (time) in place of one I in LYRICIST, and 'dancing' rearranges the result. Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC celebrity ballroom show, usually just called Strictly.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly is the everyday British name for Strictly Come Dancing, a hit BBC dance contest.

clue.text: Foul's legal — linesman's heading off

indicators.note: off means removed, so that letter goes from the word

parts.note: lawful means legal

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of linesman's

explanation.surface: A football row: the foul was legal, as the linesman heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' gives L from linesman's, and 'off' removes it from LAWFUL (legal). 'Foul' looks like a football foul; it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and foul both describe something extremely unpleasant or bad.

clue.text: Sushi: meant to be prepared with relish

indicators.note: to be prepared means to be made ready like a dish, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Sushi intended to be made and served with a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a sauce to go with the sushi; it is the definition, meaning keen enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish is great enjoyment or zest, as in tackling a task with eagerness.

clue.text: Safe getting hot as Venus in the Louvre

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the Venus de Milo statue in the Louvre is famous for having no arms

explanation.surface: A security update: the safe is warm and the statue in Paris is unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo in the Louvre museum in Paris has lost both its arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmless poses no danger, so it is safe.

clue.text: Official Aussie pick-up counter

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a match official
ute, short for utility vehicle, is Australian slang for a pick-up truck

explanation.surface: An Australian match official driving a pick-up truck to the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a noun, the shop kind; it is the verb meaning to argue against.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute an argument is to counter it by proving it false.

clue.text: Putting two lots of uranium into affected corpuscles is dim!

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium, so two lots give a pair

explanation.surface: A mad scientist injecting uranium into blood cells, which is not bright.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding two Us (uranium) to the letters of CORPUSCLES and rearranging them, as 'affected' signals, gives the answer. The exclamation suggests the experiment is stupid, which also hints at the sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepuscular light is twilight, so this rare adjective means dim or shadowy.

clue.text: End cut off cob stuffed with Parmesan cheese

indicators.note: stuffed means ruined, done for, so the letters are thrown into disorder
end cut off means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Trimming a loaf and filling it with Parmesan cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End cut off' shortens cob, a round British loaf, to CO; that and PARMESAN are rearranged, as 'stuffed' signals. Parmesan looks like the definition; it is fodder for a different cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft, creamy Italian cheese used in tiramisu.

clue.text: Marine fish in abandoned clay

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: the marlin is a large sea fish with a spear-like snout

explanation.surface: A sea fish found lying in abandoned clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the fish; it is the letters that 'abandoned' takes from MARLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Marl is a crumbly mix of clay and lime, used as fertiliser.

clue.text: Oval's pitch initially breaking up till ice melted

indicators.note: breaking up means splitting the other letters apart, so the single letter goes between them
melted means turned liquid, so the letters lose their shape and are rearranged
initially asks for the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter of pitch

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the Oval's pitch is breaking up until the ice has melted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oval' looks like the London cricket ground, and 'pitch' like its playing strip; 'Oval' is the definition and 'initially' takes only the first letter of pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is an oval curve, so the adjective describing it means oval-shaped.

clue.text: Notice soldiers pinching one's bottom

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing or nipping, so the letter is held between the others

parts.note: a poster is a notice put up in public
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers in the British army
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A sign warning that soldiers are pinching someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for other ranks, the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers. 'Pinching' fits the cheeky surface as well as the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A posterior is a humorous word for the buttocks, a person's behind.

clue.text: Church head one books into rave for a game

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Church

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so those letters go within the other word

parts.note: a rage is a craze, the latest rave
the Roman numeral I is one
B is the abbreviation for book, so two give BB

explanation.surface: A church leader books someone into a wild party for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rave' looks like a party, but here it is a craze, the latest rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by moving pegs on a board.

clue.text: Opera section with city situation

parts.note: a scena is an elaborate solo scene in an opera
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil

explanation.surface: Part of an opera combined with a city, describing a staging plan.
explanation.walkthrough: A scena is a dramatic operatic solo, a term most solvers meet only in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a possible sequence of events or state of affairs.

clue.text: Frame in which beauty pageant winner appears?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sliding frame holding the glass of a window

definitions.text: in which beauty pageant winner appears?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ribbon worn across the body by a pageant winner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' sounds as if the winner appears in a photograph frame; both halves are separate meanings of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sliding window frame and also a broad ribbon worn over one shoulder, as by a pageant winner.

clue.text: Wonder if a motorhome's possessed by a Spice girl?

indicators.note: possessed by means held within, so those letters go inside the name

parts.note: Mel B and Mel C were both members of the 1990s pop group the Spice Girls
RV, recreational vehicle, is a motorhome

explanation.surface: Imagining a camper van owned by a pop star from the Spice Girls.
explanation.walkthrough: RV, recreational vehicle, is the American term for a motorhome; the Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group with two members called Mel.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is a wonder, something causing astonishment, and both words also work as verbs.

clue.text: A fibre carpet used to make flatpack kit, say

indicators.note: used means put to work, so these letters are consumed and reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Fibres from a carpet being used to make furniture kits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to make' sounds like the start of the definition, but 'used' is the anagram signal and 'to' a link; the definition starts at 'make'.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefabricate is to manufacture sections in a factory for assembly elsewhere, as with flatpack furniture.

clue.text: US state not allowed to mock

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
out means not allowed, as in a ruling that something is out

explanation.surface: A US state that bans mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Flout is often confused with flaunt; here it has its older sense of scorning openly.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout is to openly disregard or treat with contempt, an old sense close to jeering or scoffing.

clue.text: Nut-covered Latin dish

indicators.note: covered means wrapped around, so the outer word encloses the letter

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan

explanation.surface: A Latin American dish topped with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like a nut topping; it means a devotee, FAN, which 'covered' wraps around L (Latin).
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling, served as a dish.

clue.text: Wow, performing with a cigar!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
on means performing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at someone on stage smoking a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British slang exclamation, similar to 'gosh' or 'wow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a type of cigar, long and straight with a rounded end.

clue.text: Very into fancy lingerie but right off sweet-talk

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the letter goes within the other letters
fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are worked into a new pattern
off means removed, so that letter leaves the pool

explanation.surface: Someone very keen on fancy underwear, but rudely charming someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' takes R (right) out of LINGERIE, 'fancy' rearranges the remaining letters into INEIGLE, and 'into' puts V (very) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle someone is to coax or persuade them by flattery or deception.

clue.text: Expert: 'Nessie is mostly brass'

indicators.note: is mostly means most of the letters of these words form the answer, not all

parts.note: the last four letters of expert and the first four of Nessie

explanation.surface: An expert declares the Loch Ness Monster to be made largely of brass.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass, in British slang, means cheek or impudence. Nessie is the Loch Ness Monster of Scottish legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass in the sense of brazen nerve is close to cheekiness, impudence.

clue.text: Cat circling a rocking lead vocalist's equipment

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the outer word surrounds the others

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of rocking

explanation.surface: A rock band's lead singer has kit with a cat on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead vocalist' looks like a unit; 'lead' takes R from rocking, and the definition is 'vocalist's equipment'. 'Circling' puts A and R inside LYNX.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat holds the vocal cords that a singer uses.
